title: Does Tokenization Shape Which Features Form? Spelling Features Across Tokenizers

original_idea.body:
# Does Tokenization Shape Which Features Form? Spelling Features Across Tokenizers

**Problem:** How much character-level feature cleanliness depends on tokenizer granularity is under-examined.

**Direction:** Compare spelling/first-letter feature quality between models with different tokenization granularity using pretrained SAEs or activation probing. Measure how cleanly first-letter info is linearly decodable per model.

**Why it matters:** Tokenization is an under-appreciated determinant of what models represent and how interpretable they are.

**Relevant context:** Chanin et al. 2024 absorption first-letter probes; byte-level vs BPE differences.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Vague impact: tokenizer effects on feature cleanliness are interesting but the chain to catastrophic AI risk is broad and indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Linear probing across tokenizers; guided, but cross-model probing without matched SAEs adds some difficulty.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first-letter-decodability comparison; some dependency on finding matched models/SAEs.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Fresh open interp angle labs deprioritize; public models.

novelty.reasoning: Tokenizer-granularity effects on spelling-feature cleanliness appear under-examined.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Tokenizer-granularity effects on spelling-feature cleanliness appear under-examined.
